_why: Which parts of the canonical replay document BOTH sides can produce today.
The differential layer lands module by module: curve_ref.py mirrors auction.rs, settle_ref.py
mirrors settle.rs and finalize_round, claims_ref.py mirrors claims.rs and claim_withdraw. The
Python side has all three; the Rust side has whichever replays exist.
Entries are PATHS, not whole sections, and that granularity is load-bearing rather than
fussy. claims_ref returns per_bidder AND withdraw_claims: the first is claim_payout and
claim_refund, which are DEV3's and exist; the second is claim_withdraw, which is DEV1's, and
it needs pps from a settle replay that does not exist yet. Declaring the whole section would
claim coverage of a half nobody has replayed - the silent-subset defect this file exists to
Self-checking in both directions: run_vectors.py --out emits exactly these paths, and
test_vectors.rs asserts that what it emits is exactly these paths. Adding a Rust replay
without widening this list fails the Rust test; widening it without the replay fails the diff.
To widen: add the path here in the same commit as the Rust replay that produces it.

not_yet_replayed_in_rust.settle_ref: needs finalize_round driven from a Rust replay - DEV1/DEV2
not_yet_replayed_in_rust.claims_ref.withdraw_claims: needs claim_withdraw (DEV1's) and pps from a settle replay; DEV3 computing the formula here would be a third derivation that nothing diffs
